title: Prevent refresh credentials from crossing session boundaries

critical_conclusion.action: Add generation ownership before response side effects.
critical_conclusion.consequence: An old refresh response can contaminate a new login without ownership checks.

source_inspection: Read-only exact-source review. No source changes or test execution.
facts: The refresh request record has access-token and controller fields. It has no session generation.
The success handler writes refresh headers before any ownership check.
The error handler can clear the active session after an old expired-token error.
SET_TOKEN preserves refresh credentials. The reducer assertion requires this behavior for access rotation.
Fresh login and access extension share handleLogin. They need different boundary behavior.
Axios has one registered request interceptor in current source.
Installed Axios supports synchronous request interceptors.
The shared service instance is exported. Registration-level stamping covers its current direct callers.
getRefreshToken currently swallows rejection. Home currently ignores its result.
decision: Use a module generation. Keep it independent from access-token rotation.
Stamp every request synchronously before Axios dispatch.
Advance generation at fresh-login request start and clear refresh credentials.
Advance generation again when a fresh-login response supplies access credentials.
The second boundary rejects old-access requests started during pending login.
Advance generation before logout clears storage.
Reject stale success and error results before every store mutation.
Keep controller identity checks in final cleanup.
Keep access-token equality as a deduplication key only.
Expose a current-generation pending promise for Timeout. Do not start acquisition from that helper.
Return Promise<void> consistently. Propagate acquisition failure to recovery consumers.
integration_notes: The helper has no application imports. This avoids service and logout utility cycles.
Keep generic Axios type parameters D and P. The installed Axios definitions include both.
The success guard must precede handleDrawers, handleEntities, handleUser, handleLogin, and handleRefreshToken.
The error guard must precede TOKEN_INVALID_EXPIRED handling and loader dispatch.
Use the existing reducer actions. Do not add generation side effects inside reducers.
A failed login retains the previous access state. Its cleared refresh token can be acquired again.
A successful login clears refresh again. Requests created during login cannot contaminate that session.
Do not increment generation for extend, relogin, validate, or SET_TOKEN.
getPendingRefreshToken must not require access-token equality. Same-session extension can rotate access.
The synchronous registration requires every active request interceptor to remain synchronous.
Future asynchronous interceptors require dispatch-time metadata capture instead.
Timeout integration belongs to the sibling blocker proposal.
The acquisition snippet retains its existing expiry branch. The comment marks that unchanged branch explicitly.

rejected_shortcuts.reason: Abort cannot establish ownership for already queued success or error callbacks.

rejected_shortcuts.proposal: Compare current and captured access tokens before applying refresh.
rejected_shortcuts.reason: Access extension rotates access within the same session.
This removes valid refresh credentials during same-session rotation.

rejected_shortcuts.proposal: Stamp generation in the existing asynchronous request interceptor.
rejected_shortcuts.reason: An old request could receive a new generation after a boundary.

rejected_shortcuts.proposal: Advance generation only when login starts.
rejected_shortcuts.reason: Old-access acquisition during pending login could survive into the new session.

rejected_shortcuts.proposal: Clear the whole session when login starts.
rejected_shortcuts.reason: This changes failed-login behavior beyond the needed refresh fix.

required_verification: Hold A refresh success. Logout, then login B. Deliver A success. Assert B refresh remains unchanged.
Deliver old expired-token error after B login. Assert B remains authenticated.
Start A refresh while B login is pending. Complete B login first. Assert A refresh is rejected.
Complete the pending A refresh first. Then complete B login. Assert B starts without A refresh.
Start two fresh logins. Complete them in reverse order. Assert only the current attempt installs credentials.
Rotate access with extend during one session. Assert refresh remains available.
Complete a same-session acquisition after access rotation. Assert epoch ownership remains valid.
Abort an old acquisition. Start a replacement. Assert old cleanup preserves the replacement record.
Reject a current acquisition. Assert Timeout sees rejection and Home has no unhandled rejection.
Check future interceptor registration. Assert generation capture still occurs before a logout boundary.
limits: No snippet was applied, typechecked, built, or executed.
This design does not prove server revocation, rotation, or refresh contract behavior.
The late-response expectation is source-based review inference. It has no independent approved policy source.
No new PROD recommendation follows from this proposal alone.
Synchronous registration changes dispatch timing. Verify current service consumers before applying.
A separately created Axios instance is outside this shared interceptor protection.
Cross-tab coordination is outside the demonstrated single-page race.

limitations: Automated checks do not check the complete approved dictionary or grammar rules.
